solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oral health specialist employing intense daylight

indicators.note: employing means putting to use, so the letters of the two words are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A dentist's assistant who works under a fierce bright light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employing' looks like a link joining definition and wordplay, but it signals the rearrangement of all fifteen letters of 'intense daylight'.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional cleans teeth and advises on gum care, a specialist in the health of the mouth.

clue.text: Rather shabby, like your setter, naturally!

definitions.meaning: a book with folded-over page corners looks worn and tatty
a setter is a breed of dog, so it naturally has a dog's ears

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that they look a little worn out, as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your setter' seems to mean the compiler, Crux, but read it as the gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Books with turned-down page corners look scruffy, so the word means worn and tatty.

clue.text: Leading painkiller, you might say

parts.note: something that numbs pain could jokingly be called a numb-er, and the top one would be first in the chart

explanation.surface: A recommendation for the most popular analgesic on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the six-letter word as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs, and the best painkiller is the top numb-er.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means first or foremost, the top of a list or chart.

clue.text: Too partial in a trial sometimes

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A remark that legal proceedings can sometimes be biased too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: Therapeutic waterworks?

parts.note: waterworks is slang for tears, and having tears flow can make one feel better

explanation.surface: Seemingly a question about a healing spa or water treatment plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on the waterworks' is British slang for starting to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A long weep that leaves one feeling better is said to be cathartic, a healing release of tears.

clue.text: Prisoner's possible goal — to take a hobby, say

indicators.note: the letters of goal give only a possible version of it, one rearranged

parts.note: the hobby is a small falcon, an example of a bird

explanation.surface: An inmate's hope of taking up a pastime while inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' looks like a pastime but is the falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for a convict, especially a habitual one who spends long spells inside.

clue.text: Chance features very largely in western

definitions.text: Chance features very largely in western

parts.words: Chance features very largely in western
parts.note: a synonym of chance, accident or accidental, appears almost whole inside the word meaning western

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that luck plays a big part in a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' looks like a cowboy film but is the adjective; the word for chance, ACCIDENTAL, lies very largely (all but its first letter) inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the West, so the adjective means relating to western countries.

clue.text: Cold country, we're told repeatedly, for hot food

indicators.note: two words heard alike in turn: cold is chilly, and the country sounds the same

parts.note: chilly (cold) and Chile (the South American country) sound alike

explanation.surface: A traveller keeps hearing about a chilly land, yet finds spicy dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Chilly (cold) and Chile (the country) both sound like the spicy dish, hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy stew of meat and beans flavoured with hot peppers, a fiery dish.

clue.text: Most agreeable chaps, you'd think, but real creeps

definitions.meaning: men who always say yes seem to agree with everything
sycophants who flatter the boss are toadies

explanation.surface: A judgement on men who seem pleasant but are actually unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who agree with everything a superior says, flattering underlings.

clue.text: Finally out of time for a Greek god

indicators.note: the letter for time is taken out of the phrase meaning finally

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: Time at last runs out for an ancient deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan of Greek myth who holds up the sky on his shoulders.

clue.text: Spirited defence clinches English striker's ultimate triumph

parts.note: game means brave and spirited

indicators.note: to clinch is to hold tight, so the defence wraps round the letter for English

parts.note: a stand is a defensive stance, as in a last stand
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A football report: a gutsy defence and an English centre forward win the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer but is a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpire's call at the end of a tennis match signals complete and final victory.

clue.text: Some large flowers, maybe, or little ones mentioned

indicators.note: the words are spoken, and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: little ones are kids, so the words sound like or kids

explanation.surface: A choice between big blooms or small ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic plants with showy blooms; some species bear big flowers.

clue.text: Heads lose carbon copies

indicators.note: the headlands drop the symbol for carbon

parts.note: heads are headlands, also called capes
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Office managers do without carbon copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copies' looks like one phrase, but carbon belongs to the wordplay and copies is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to mimic or imitate, so the verb means imitates.

clue.text: Its sharp points are essential in fencing

definitions.text: Its sharp points are essential in fencing

parts.words: Its sharp points are essential in fencing
parts.note: fencing here is building fences, not swordplay, and this barrier relies on spikes

explanation.surface: Seemingly about the sharp tip of a foil in the sport of fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiked strands of twisted steel used for farm and security barriers.

clue.text: Doctor recalled in fairy tale

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician is summoned back in a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, a medic; it is a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic story of a girl, a pumpkin coach and a glass slipper.

clue.text: On reflection, it's at the heart of sexual love

indicators.note: seen in a mirror, the letters run backwards
the word it sits at, within, the heart

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
it, taken as written

explanation.surface: A thoughtful lover concludes that desire lies at the centre of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' supplies just IT, its 's read as 'is'; 'heart' looks like part of the love theme but gives the word for a centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sexual desire or passion.

clue.text: Al dente meal (no starter) is within call

indicators.note: the trimmed meal is placed within the word for call

parts.note: to cry is to call out

indicators.note: the meal loses its first letter, as a dinner might lose its first course

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: A pasta dish served without an appetiser is being ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' removes the L of LUNCH, leaving UNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta cooked al dente is still firm to the bite, with a slight crispness.

clue.text: See 1 across
Careless men with woman who wants a reminder

indicators.note: careless suggests the letters are arranged carelessly, out of order
wants means lacks, so the name lacks the letter a

parts.note: Monica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A forgetful woman wants a memory aid because the men are careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless' rearranges MEN to MNE; 'who wants a' takes A off MONICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme or memory aid, a device to help recall something.

clue.text: Smart Alec's packaged underwear?

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
something packaged is in a box

explanation.surface: A joke about a know-all's underclothes coming boxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A very clever person, a know-all who flaunts their intelligence.

clue.text: The council finally close such libraries

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of council

parts.note: a close is an end or ending

explanation.surface: A complaint that the council is shutting public libraries.
explanation.definitionFit: Public libraries that loan out books are known by this term.

clue.text: Harry displays logo on back of jumper

parts.note: a badge is an emblem or logo

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Prince Harry displays a crest on his sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince but is a verb; a jumper is a British sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester, harass and nag repeatedly.

clue.text: Gold found in North Sea causes upset

indicators.note: the gold symbol is found in the abbreviated sea

parts.note: N for north plus sea
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gold find in the North Sea causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach queasiness, a feeling of sickness as in an upset stomach.

clue.text: Shows derision, or its opposite when church opens

indicators.note: the abbreviation for church opens the word for its opposite, in place of the first letter

parts.note: the opposite of booing a performer is cheering them

explanation.surface: Booing gives way to applause when the church service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of jeering is cheering; swap CH, church, at the front for J to return to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff and mock someone loudly, a crowd's taunts.

clue.text: A grandma (me!) appropriately mixed up letters

definitions.text: A grandma (me!) appropriately mixed up letters

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A grandmother admits she shuffled letters around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriately' signals that the clue describes itself: the shuffled letters of 'A grandma me' make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranged letters to form a new word, as crossword setters do.

clue.text: It's accepted, say, for all to hear

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: accepted means allowed

explanation.surface: Something has been publicly accepted and announced.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken out so that everyone can hear, audibly.

clue.text: Possibly a hairy creature still needs one

parts.note: still means yet, as in yet to come
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hairy animal still needs one more thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman, a shaggy beast of Himalayan legend, maybe real.

clue.text: Recruit wearing a light beige

indicators.note: the word recruit wears, holds within it, the letters

explanation.surface: A new soldier dressed in a pale uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale greyish-yellow colour of unbleached linen.

clue.text: With a surfeit of pride, perhaps

definitions.text: With a surfeit of pride, perhaps

parts.words: With a surfeit of pride, perhaps
parts.note: puffed up by too much pride, as in the idiom of being bloated with pride

explanation.surface: Describes someone conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'swollen with pride'; 'perhaps' signals other things can make one puffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged or puffed up, here figuratively by excess conceit.

clue.text: Brief record a member makes to scale — again

indicators.note: a brief version of the word is cut short

parts.note: record gives RECORD, here shortened
a limb such as an arm or leg is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A short note about a band member making a recording to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts ORD from RECORD, leaving REC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend a hill or wall a second time, climbing up once more.

clue.text: See 10
What the rich were liable to with French on duty

definitions.text: What the rich were liable to

parts.note: sur is French for on
a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: Wealthy people once had to pay French customs charges.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra levy once charged on high incomes above a set threshold.
